properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 10 at 2:46AM CDT by NWS Sioux Falls SD
properties.description:
South winds gusting as high as 40 to 45 mph will develop quickly
by mid to late morning. Wind speeds will ease across east-central
South Dakota by mid afternoon, while the stronger gusts linger in
southwest Minnesota through sunset.

These strong winds, combined with near-record warmth and humidity
levels as low as 25 to 35 percent, will produce elevated fire
weather concerns today. Grassland fire danger will reach the High
category, with locally higher fire danger in cured croplands and
grasses.

Avoid outdoor burning and use extra caution with equipment in dry
crops, as rapid fire spread is possible.

In addition to the elevated fire danger, winds gusting over 40 mph
may produce areas of blowing dust, locally reducing visibility and
air quality.

The National Weather Service in Jacksonville has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Altamaha Sound GA to Fernandina Beach FL from 20 to 60
NM...

Tug Rio Caroni, or 21 nm south of R2 Tower, moving north at 50

properties.instruction:

jack lines and harnesses if available. Check life saving equipment,
including batteries on handheld radios, for readiness.

properties.headline: Frost Advisory issued October 10 at 12:41AM PDT until October 11 at 9:00AM PDT by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...For both Frost Advisories, temperatures as low as 33 to 36
degrees will result in frost formation.

* WHERE...Upper Hood River Valley County, especially near Parkdale.

* WHEN...For the first Frost Advisory, until 9 AM PDT this morning.
For the second Frost Advisory, from midnight tonight to 9 AM PDT
Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Frost could harm sensitive outdoor vegetation. Sensitive
outdoor plants may be killed if left uncovered.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Chances for sub-freezing temperatures below 32
degrees are high in Parkdale and Dee (70-90%) Saturday night into
Sunday morning. However, the majority of the Upper Hood River
Valley should remain above freezing with lows of 33 to 36 degrees,
including in Odell.
properties.instruction:
Take steps now to protect tender outdoor plants from the cold.
Consider temporarily moving outdoor potted plants indoors if they are
sensitive to cold temperatures.

Consider temporarily covering sensitive plants with a lightweight
cotton fabric (i.e., bedsheets, thin blankets), as this will help
retain heat and provide frost protection for your plants.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 10 at 3:36AM EDT until October 10 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and large breaking waves expected.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...Pinellas and Coastal Hillsborough Counties.

* WHEN...For the the Coastal Flood Advisory, through 8 AM EDT this
morning. For the High Surf Risk, through 8 PM EDT this evening.
For the Rip Current Risk, through Sunday evening.


* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 10 at 3:35AM EDT until October 10 at 12:45PM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Coffee County in southeastern Alabama...
Western Dale County in southeastern Alabama...
Geneva County in southeastern Alabama...

* WHEN...Until 1145 AM CDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads
remain closed due to flooding. Streams continue to rise due to
excess runoff from earlier rainfall. It will take several hours for
all the water from these storms to work through local drainage
systems in urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 232 AM CDT, Extremely heavy rain on Friday night due to
Hurricane Isaias brought 5 to 12 inches of rain to the warned
area. Heavy rain has ended, but small streams, creeks and rivers
will continue to rise and flood for at least several more hours
as water moves downhill and downstream.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Daleville, Elba, Enterprise, Fort Rucker, Geneva, Ozark, Level
Plains, Samson, New Brockton, Ariton, Lee, Clayhatchee, Kinston,
Coffee Springs, Enterprise Municipal A/P, Turner Crossroads,
Battens Crossroads, Lucile and Shell Army Field.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING IN EFFECT UNTIL 1145 AM CDT THIS MORNING

properties.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued October 10 at 2:28AM CDT by NWS Jackson MS
properties.description:
HLSJAN

This product covers Central Mississippi, Northeast Louisiana, and extreme Southeast Arkansas

**Tropical Storm Warning Is Canceled But Gusty Winds Remain A
Concern Today**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- All watches and warnings have been canceled

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 220 miles east-southeast of Jackson MS
- 31.5N 86.5W
- Storm Intensity 65 mph
- Movement North or 355 degrees at 20 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin yesterday evening and has
since weakened to a Post-Tropical Cyclone moving north through the
region. Heavy rainfall and gusty winds remain a concern for portions
of our forecast area today. A Wind Advisory and a Flash Flood Watch are
in effect for those affected areas.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Little to no impacts are anticipated at this time across Central
Mississippi, Northeast Louisiana, and extreme Southeast Arkansas.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Little to no impacts are anticipated at this time across Central
Mississippi, Northeast Louisiana, and extreme Southeast Arkansas.

* TORNADOES:
Little to no impacts are anticipated at this time across Central
Mississippi, Northeast Louisiana, and extreme Southeast Arkansas.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:

If your home or shelter was damaged, be cautious around electrical
wiring, broken glass, jagged metal and wood, and protruding nails and
screws.

Be alert for any lingering wind gusts which could take down weakened
trees and/or power lines, collapse damaged structures, or cause
flying debris.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

As it pertains to this event...this will be the last local statement
issued by the National Weather Service in Jackson MS regarding the
effects of tropical cyclone hazards upon the area.

NWSheadline:
Tropical Storm Warning Is Canceled But Gusty Winds Remain A

properties.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued October 10 at 2:20AM CDT by NWS Memphis TN
properties.description:
HLSMEG

This product covers Mid-South

**THE REMNANTS OF ISAIAS WILL CONTINUE TO MOVE NORTH OVERNIGHT**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- All watches and warnings have been canceled

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 320 miles southeast of Memphis TN or about 230 miles
southeast of Tupelo MS
- 31.5N 86.5W
- Storm Intensity 65 mph
- Movement North or 355 degrees at 20 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Hurricane Isaias made landfall around 8:30 PM CDT this evening near
Destin, FL and quickly became post-tropical. Its remnants will move
inland through Saturday, bringing gusty winds and heavy rainfall across
portions of the Mid-South. A wind advisory will replace the Tropical
Storm Warning and a flooding threat continues.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Protect against hazardous wind having possible limited impacts across
northeast Mississippi. Potential impacts in this area include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

Elsewhere across Mid-South, little to no impact is anticipated.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Protect against dangerous rainfall flooding having possible significant
impacts across northeast Mississippi. Potential impacts include:
- Moderate rainfall flooding may prompt several evacuations and
rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly become swollen with swifter
currents and overspill their banks in a few places, especially
in usually vulnerable spots. Small streams, creeks, canals,
arroyos, and ditches overflow.
- Flood waters can enter some structures or weaken foundations.
Several places may experience expanded areas of rapid
inundation at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage
areas. Some streets and parking lots take on moving water as
storm drains and retention ponds overflow. Driving conditions
become hazardous. Some road and bridge closures.

Protect against locally hazardous rainfall flooding having possible
limited impacts across northeast Mississippi.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Memphis TN as conditions warrant.
